question: Hemis festival is associated with which of the following religions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhism**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hemis festival** is a significant religious festival in **Buddhism**, celebrated in the Hemis Monastery in Ladakh, India.
 
• This festival marks the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava, who is believed to be the founder of Tibetan Buddhism.
 
• The celebrations include colorful masked dances, traditional music, and various cultural performances that attract both locals and tourists.
 
• The festival is held annually in the fifth month of the Tibetan lunar calendar, which usually falls in June or July.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Hemis Monastery** is one of the largest and wealthiest monasteries in Ladakh, founded by King Sengge Namgyal in 1672.
 
• The monastery is known for its rich collection of ancient relics, thangkas (Tibetan Buddhist paintings), and statues.
 
• The Hemis festival provides a glimpse into the rich cultural heritage and religious traditions of the Tibetan Buddhist community in Ladakh.
 
• Visitors to the festival can also explore the beautiful landscapes and unique architecture of the region.
